tables.title: Bayesian Pearson Correlations
notes: Prior: stretched beta on ρ with width 0.333.

interpretation.text:
Bayesian correlation tests (Ly, Verhagen & Wagenmakers, 2016):

mpg and wt (r = −0.87, n = 32): BF₁₀ = 1.33 × 10⁷, extreme evidence for H₁.

mpg and qsec (r = 0.42, n = 32): BF₁₀ = 4.42, moderate evidence for H₁.

wt and qsec (r = −0.17, n = 32): BF₁₀ = 0.576, anecdotal evidence for H₀.

title: Bayesian Correlation
code:
library(BayesFactor)
library(ggnext)
rscale <- 1 / 3   # width of the stretched beta prior on rho
# mpg and wt
d_1 <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("mpg", "wt")]), c("mpg", "wt")]
bf_1 <- correlationBF(d_1$mpg, d_1$wt, rscale = rscale)
set.seed(123)
rho_1 <- as.numeric(posterior(bf_1, iterations = 10000, progress = FALSE)[, "rho"])

# mpg and qsec
d_2 <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("mpg", "qsec")]), c("mpg", "qsec")]
bf_2 <- correlationBF(d_2$mpg, d_2$qsec, rscale = rscale)
set.seed(123)
rho_2 <- as.numeric(posterior(bf_2, iterations = 10000, progress = FALSE)[, "rho"])

# wt and qsec
d_3 <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("wt", "qsec")]), c("wt", "qsec")]
bf_3 <- correlationBF(d_3$wt, d_3$qsec, rscale = rscale)
set.seed(123)
rho_3 <- as.numeric(posterior(bf_3, iterations = 10000, progress = FALSE)[, "rho"])
p <- ggnext(d_1, aes(mpg, wt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "mpg and wt", x = "Miles per US gallon", y = "Weight (1000 lbs)") +
  theme_modern()
